[42828 Introduction to Agent Based Modelling | Subject description]
Credit points: 3

This microcredential equips you with the skills to construct and adapt simulation models for complex systems, whose emergent properties are unpredictable due to the interplay of their elements. You'll delve into Agent-Based Modelling (ABM) and Agent-Based Modelling and Simulation (ABMS), practical methodologies for exploring and understanding the intricate dynamics of complex systems.

[42828 Introduction to Agent Based Modelling | Learning and teaching activities]
This microcredential uses supported online learning strategies. Self-paced online learning material, including appropriate readings and videos, introduce concepts of systems and complex systems.

 Case studies help develop the concepts, techniques of modelling, and the techniques of using ABM. Engaging with real models and modelling tools such as NetLogo builds skills of modelling with ABM and of analysing the outcomes of such modelling. This analysis develops the awareness of the assumptions and limitations generally inherent in any modelling effort.

 Weekly asynchronous online consultations at times nominated on the LMS used (e.g. Canvas) and moderated discussion boards enable clarification of issues and peer/expert support for learning. Feedback on assessments, both automated and human, will also be available through the LMS.

title: Learning outcomes
content:
[42828 Introduction to Agent Based Modelling | Learning outcomes]
SLO1: Characterize complex systems to identify elements suitable for development of ABMs to simulate the system interactions and characteristics. (D.1)
SLO2: Design and assess the impact of modifications to an existing complex system’s ABM. (C.1)
SLO3: Use reflection strategies to enhance students’ understanding and contribution to modelling practice. (F.1)
